newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state offers stake in housing firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state offers stake in housing firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema on Monday offered investors a minimum 20 percent stake in partly-private unit Cairo Housing and Development.
The firm said in a published advertisement that the public offer of at least 1.272 million shares will be open for five days from March 12.
The share offer price will be the market price of the stocks listed on the Cairo bourse at the end of trading on March 11. The stock last traded on Monday at around 24.7 pounds ($7.27).
Individuals should apply for at least 100 shares, while mutual funds and private firms have a 10,000 share minimum. National Societe General Bank and Triple A Securities are the agents for the offer.
Brokers said in July 1996 that privatised realty rival Medinet Nasr Housing and Development had bought a controlling 65 percent stake in Cairo Housing but the deal was refused.
The state then said it would offer a 40 percent stake in the firm late last year but reversed the decision.

The advertisement said that private investors hold 17.35 percent, banks and public-sector firms 7.65 percent and the firm's employee shareholder association 10 percent of Cairo Housing and Development.

The holding firm said Cairo Housing and Development raised net after-tax profit to 5.355 million pounds in financial 1995/96 from 2.947 million pounds in the previous year. It expects the profit to increase to 10.624 million in 1996/97.
The financial year ends on June 30.
The holding company said new shareholders would receive the 1996/97 dividend of 1.00 pound per share. The firm distributed 0.53 pounds in 1995/96.

Real estate firms have proved popular with investors and their soaring share prices have helped fuel the bourse's recent rallies. Last May, the state sold off 70 percent of Medinet Nasr for 65 pounds a share. The stock was trading on Sunday at 517.70.
